clue.text: Element divider flexibly accommodating ununoctium (the last)

definitions.text: Element divider flexibly accommodating ununoctium (the last)

indicators.note: the shuffled letters take in and hold the extra one, a container signal
the letters bend into a new shape, so the two words are rearranged
points to the closing letter of the element's name, its M

explanation.surface: A chemist who sorted the elements makes room for a newly made heavy element at the end of his table.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: the Russian chemist divided the elements into his periodic table, and ununoctium (element 118) sat last in it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Russian chemist devised the periodic table, grouping the chemical elements into rows and columns.

clue.text: Cheers solvers are barred from getting

parts.note: the setter addresses the people solving, second person
a modal saying something is forbidden to you, the contracted ought-not form
getting means receiving or possessing, as in have

explanation.surface: A toast that seems to tell solvers they will be denied something.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, the phrase says the solvers ought not to receive something; as a whole it is the polite protest on being given a present.
explanation.definitionFit: Said on receiving a gift, the phrase is a way of saying thank you, as cheers is in British English.

clue.text: Redevelopment of East End integral to total object of perception

indicators.note: being integral to something means sitting inside it, so the shuffled letters go within

parts.note: a total is a sum

indicators.note: redeveloping rebuilds the place, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Regenerating London's East End is a key part of a larger whole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'integral to' puts SENSEDAT, the rearranged EAST END, inside SUM. The East End is the historically working-class eastern part of London.
explanation.definitionFit: In philosophy, this term names the immediate content of a perception, such as a patch of colour seen.

clue.text: Very impressive visit without telephone

indicators.note: here in its old sense of outside, so the visit wraps around the phone

parts.note: a visit is a stay somewhere

explanation.surface: An impressive visit made without bringing a phone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like lacking, but in its old sense of outside it makes STAY surround TEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something grand and dignified in appearance, like a fine house, is described as majestic or imposing.

clue.text: A couple one bumped into on the rebound?

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: bouncing back, so the word for bumped into is read backwards

parts.note: bumping into someone is meeting them, past tense met

explanation.surface: A pair who got together after one of them had just been dumped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the rebound' also has its romantic sense of a new relationship after a breakup, which suits a couple.
explanation.definitionFit: Two people romantically linked are informally called an item, an established pair.

clue.text: So makeshift team did it at last?

definitions.meaning: roughly assembled from whatever was to hand
a team of shoemakers working at the last, the foot-shaped block, did it jointly

explanation.surface: A team finally managed something, but only in a rough-and-ready way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at last' looks like finally; a last is the shoemaker's foot-shaped block, so a team of shoemakers did the job side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Something put together hastily and crudely is described this way, an idiom for improvised.

clue.text: Its members say they've made it up

definitions.text: Its members say they've made it up

parts.words: Its members say they've made it up
parts.note: members of this informal club claim to have had sex aboard an aircraft in flight, high in the air

explanation.surface: A club whose members may be inventing their claims.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made it up' looks like lying, but here it is having sex way up in the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: The jocular name for people who claim to have had sex on board a plane in flight.

clue.text: Dispensing with loving gestures, thugs pin me to ground, helpless

indicators.note: ground as in crushed, so the remaining letters are pounded into a new order
doing without, so those letters are removed from the word before it

parts.note: hugs are loving gestures

explanation.surface: Thugs with no tenderness pin someone to the floor, leaving them powerless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dispensing with' takes HUGS out of thugs, leaving T; 'ground' then rearranges T plus PINMETO.
explanation.definitionFit: Powerless or unable to act effectively, a synonym of helpless.

clue.text: Cup replay's final touch by Hearts left back

indicators.note: one piece sits touching the next, joined side by side
reading back turns the word for left around

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
H is the abbreviation for the card suit hearts

indicators.note: the closing letter of replay is used

explanation.surface: A football report: a cup replay settled at the last by Hearts' left-back.
explanation.walkthrough: Hearts is a Scottish football club and a left-back a defender, so the surface reads as match commentary.
explanation.definitionFit: A cup is a common kind of trophy, a prize awarded to winners.

clue.text: Secret police force's arrest

parts.note: the Stasi was the East German secret police
the possessive ending supplies its letter

explanation.surface: An arrest carried out by a secret police force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrest' looks like detention by police, but here it is the noun for stopping or halting.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrest is a stopping of motion or progress, and the answer is a state of stagnation or standstill.

clue.text: Mob wants me to go off in a while, having retreated?

definitions.text: Mob wants me to go off in a while, having retreated?

indicators.note: the shuffled letters sit inside the reversed word
gone backwards, so the word for a while is reversed

parts.note: a while is a bit, as in wait a bit

indicators.note: going off as an explosion scatters the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A speaker says the gang wants them to explode after a delay, once it has pulled back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go off' looks like leave but means explode. 'having retreated' turns the word for a while round, 'to go off' shuffles the two short words, and the whole clue also pictures the device a gang plants.
explanation.definitionFit: An explosive set to detonate after a delay, timed by a clock mechanism, the kind a gang plants and then flees.

clue.text: Down-and-out, like team with such a record?

definitions.text: like team with such a record?
definitions.meaning: split, the letters read as a victory count of zero, the record of a side that has never won

explanation.surface: A team with a dismal record is down and out.
explanation.walkthrough: Break the word after its third letter: the tally reads as nil victories, a team's poor record.
explanation.definitionFit: A down-and-out alcoholic, typically one living on the streets and drinking cheap liquor.

clue.text: Hotel defamation cases during stay not a result of contaminated food

indicators.note: the combined pieces fall within the shortened stay
not the letter given next, so it is dropped

parts.note: a stay of proceedings is a delay

indicators.note: the defamation word encases the hotel letter

parts.note: libel is written defamation
Hotel is H in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A hotel faces defamation suits while guests are staying, though their illness wasn't food poisoning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not a' strips the A from the word for stay, and 'cases' has the defamation word wrap round the hotel letter. Hotel is H in the NATO alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: A jocular name for the diarrhoea travellers get from contaminated food or water abroad.

clue.text: Making merry a bit insane while away!

indicators.note: making merry with something plays about with it, so its letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Partying a bit wildly while on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'while away' looks like a verb meaning pass time idly, but it is while plus away, being absent.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin legal phrase means in someone's absence, as when a person is tried or sentenced while not present.

clue.text: Got off just over halfway through dismal government-free existence

indicators.note: the insert goes slightly past the midpoint of the three remaining letters
free of, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: grey means dull and dismal
alighted, past tense alit, as from a bus

explanation.surface: Someone escaped from a bleak, stateless life partway through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'government-free' splits one hyphenated word: the first half is the letter removed, the second the removal signal. 'just over halfway through' puts the insert after the second of three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Reality is the state of things as they actually exist, so the word serves for existence.

clue.text: Letters you see to be typed, for example S-K-I-P T-E-A

definitions.text: Letters you see to be typed

parts.note: a skip or skipper is a captain, abbreviated Capt
cha is a slang word for tea

explanation.surface: An example of a jumbled code to type in, spelt out letter by letter.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphenated words mimic the distorted characters a website shows, yet each still has to be read as a word.
explanation.definitionFit: The website test shows distorted characters a visitor must type in to prove they are human.

clue.text: Dissident went and won Hemel Hempstead?

indicators.note: a dissident breaks from the established order, so the letters break their order

explanation.surface: A rebel candidate wins a seat at Hemel Hempstead.
explanation.walkthrough: Hemel Hempstead is a Hertfordshire town expanded after the Second World War as a planned settlement; the question mark marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Hemel Hempstead is an example of a planned post-war British settlement built to rehouse people from London.

clue.text: They're not even occasional painkillers!

parts.note: odd as in occasional, now and then
read as things that numb, a numb-er being a painkiller

explanation.surface: Taking painkillers only now and then hardly counts as a regime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'painkillers' hides a second sense: things that numb, read with a silent b.
explanation.definitionFit: Integers that cannot be divided by two, like 1, 3 and 5, are the opposite of even ones.

clue.text: Grand military official's losing it

parts.note: G is slang for a grand, a thousand
an aga was an Ottoman military commander

explanation.surface: A senior military officer is going senile.
explanation.definitionFit: Losing it means losing one's wits, and the answer is slang for crazy or senile.

clue.text: Lincoln pub given the go-ahead in key letters

indicators.note: the pub and president go inside the key

parts.note: Alt is a key on a computer keyboard

indicators.note: the pub letters are allowed to go ahead, placed before the president

parts.note: PH is the map abbreviation for public house
Abe is Abraham Lincoln's nickname

explanation.surface: A pub in Lincoln gets approval in some important letters.
explanation.walkthrough: Lincoln looks like the English city but is Abraham Lincoln.
explanation.definitionFit: The alphabet is the full set of letters used to write a language.

clue.text: Vehicle heading for Hertfordshire wilderness

parts.note: a bus is a vehicle

indicators.note: the heading, the first letter, of the county is taken

explanation.surface: A bus heading into Hertfordshire's wild country.
explanation.walkthrough: Hertfordshire is an English county just north of London.
explanation.definitionFit: The bush is wild, uncultivated country, especially in Australia or Africa.

clue.text: Time allowed for preparation once varied with it

indicators.note: changed in arrangement, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Preparation time was once allowed, but things changed.
explanation.definitionFit: Advance warning gives time to get ready, as in a week's warning before leaving a job.

clue.text: Literary man's endless fun, hosting evening of poetry

indicators.note: the shortened fun hosts the evening word inside it
with its end gone, the last letter is dropped

parts.note: jest means fun or joking
eve is the poetic word for evening

explanation.surface: A writer's endless jokes at a poetry evening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts JEST to JES, which then holds EVE.
explanation.definitionFit: P. G. Wodehouse's fictional valet is a famous character of literature, gentleman's gentleman to Bertie Wooster.

clue.text: The reason solicitor's reported heavy blizzard

indicators.note: reported speech, so the words are heard rather than read

parts.note: the reason for something is the why of it; a tout solicits custom, so is a solicitor

explanation.surface: A lawyer explains why a storm was reported.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solicitor' looks like a British lawyer but is a tout, one who solicits business.
explanation.definitionFit: A weather condition where snow cuts visibility so much that land and sky blur into one.
